headline: The FBI named ARTEX, the open-source AI attack framework, as the engine behind intrusions worldwide, including a ConnectWise supply-chain breach that reached customers' Microsoft 365 environments.

emerging_trends.text: The FBI's warning that ARTEX now drives intrusions worldwide, including the ConnectWise supply-chain breach that landed inside customers' Microsoft 365 environments, moves agentic attack frameworks from research curiosity to the stated cause of named incidents.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FBI Ties ARTEX to a ConnectWise Supply-Chain Breach

emerging_trends.text: One access key that Fireworks AI exposed carried an attacker into Cursor's extension marketplace and onto developers' machines, which makes the AI infrastructure layer a single point of failure for the tools that write production code.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Stolen Fireworks Key Opened Cursor's Marketplace

emerging_trends.text: Italy's Garante priced a default-on photo gallery feature at 805 million euros the same week Apple published silicon that fences camera and microphone data off from iOS, and both moved the fight over phone sensors down to defaults and hardware.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Italy Fines Meta Over Facebook Gallery Access

topics.title: Agents Get Spending Power Before Controls Catch Up
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, built with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa, which pays merchants through a stand-in card number so a user's real card details reach neither the agent nor the merchant, and Token Security published five enterprise gaps it found while testing an invoice-processing agent that a malicious email could push into changing a vendor's bank details with no alert firing.
topics.summary: Agents now hold payment authority and finance workflows inside companies, and the identity and approval controls around them lag the capability. Token Security's guidance and OpenAI's stand-in card both aim at the same problem: an agent that acts with a person's authority and no bounded credential.

sources.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets agents pay without seeing your card number
How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps
Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity?

topics.title: Stolen Fireworks Key Opened Cursor's Marketplace
topics.latest_developments: Cursor said in a Friday, November 13, 2026 update that the attacker obtained an access key Cursor itself had issued to Fireworks AI, that Fireworks exposed the key, and that the attacker used it to copy data from a read-only source.
topics.summary: Attackers distributed a malicious version of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension through Cursor's extension marketplace, working from credentials stolen in the breach at Fireworks AI, the AI infrastructure provider. Developers who installed the extension should rotate every credential the editor could reach.

sources.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension

topics.title: Italy Fines Meta Over Facebook Gallery Access
topics.latest_developments: The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, fined Meta 805 million euros, about $887 million, on November 14, 2026, finding that Facebook for Android read Italian users' photos, videos, and related metadata without explicit consent, and gave the company 60 days.
topics.summary: Facebook for Android suggests photos and videos out of a user's phone gallery as post material, and the feature arrives switched on. The Garante cited a European directive that treats a smartphone as part of a person's private sphere and demands free and informed consent before an app reaches into it.

sources.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
Meta Fined $887 Million in Italy Over Android Gallery Photos and Videos on Facebook

topics.title: FBI Ties ARTEX to a ConnectWise Supply-Chain Breach
topics.latest_developments: The FBI warned on November 15, 2026 that attackers run ARTEX, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, to automate attacks on organizations worldwide, and pointed to a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised customers' Microsoft 365 environments as one result.
topics.summary: ARTEX chains reconnaissance, exploitation, and follow-on actions with little operator skill, and the FBI's November 13, 2026 flash alert clocked some intrusions from first targeting to privileged access in under three hours. Defenders should hunt for credential attacks running at machine speed and audit every remote monitoring and management tool, ConnectWise ScreenConnect included.

sources.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks

topics.title: TSMC Employee Data Surfaces in a 6.9GB Auction
topics.latest_developments: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company confirmed on November 15, 2026 that employee personal data reached the open internet after a threat actor auctioned 6.9 gigabytes of files the actor claimed it took from the chipmaker, and TSMC traces the records to the system services of a cloud service provider it uses.
topics.summary: TSMC, the Taiwanese foundry that fabricates chips for Apple, Nvidia, and AMD, says none of its own systems fell and that the exposed files hold employee information. Staff should expect phishing that cites accurate employment details.

sources.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider

topics.title: A 22-Year-Old PostgreSQL Bug Runs Code
topics.latest_developments: The worst flaw in this week's PostgreSQL release now carries a number and an age: CVE-2026-6460, a type confusion bug rated 8.8 that has sat in the code for 22 years and lets any database user who can create objects run commands on the server with the rights of the operating system account.
topics.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group closed 52 vulnerabilities on November 12, 2026 across versions 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25. Patching alone leaves a gap: administrators must also rebuild every C-language extension installed on the server.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE

topics.title: Pentagon Renames the CDAO
topics.latest_developments: The Department of Defense renamed its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office the Super Intelligence Office, following President Trump's order that executive branch communications replace the phrase artificial intelligence with super intelligence.
topics.summary: The CDAO runs the Pentagon's data, analytics, and AI programs, including the model evaluation and deployment work that military cyber operations draw on. The rename reaches contractors and program documents that cite the office by name.

sources.title: Pentagon Renames CDAO ‘Super Intelligence Office’

topics.title: Apple Details Secure Exclaves for Camera and Mic
topics.latest_developments: Apple published the architecture of Secure Exclaves, which isolates camera and microphone data from the main operating system on HomeView and the newest iPhones, so a compromise of iOS alone leaves ambient sensor data out of an attacker's reach.
topics.summary: Secure Exclaves fence off the hardware that watches and listens, holding that data inside a separate execution environment the general-purpose operating system cannot reach. The design matters most for always-on home devices, where a single operating system flaw would otherwise open a live camera and microphone.

sources.title: Apple Reveals How Secure Exclaves Shield Camera and Microphone Data

business_politics.title: Washington Lines Up Allies Before Shenzhen
business_politics.latest_developments: The United States and allied governments signed an accord Sunday, November 15, to protect artificial-intelligence supply chains from China, days before President Trump meets Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen.
business_politics.summary: The pact covers the chips, tools, and materials that feed artificial-intelligence computing, and it lands while Congress drafts tighter export controls after the Nvidia scandal. Trump sits down with Xi and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week, and Anthropic's New York listing arrives in the same stretch.

sources.title: US and allies sign accord to protect AI supply chains from China
Anthropic IPO to further fuel the AI news cycle

business_politics.title: The AI Trade Unravels
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, November 15, that shares in the data center construction companies at the center of the artificial-intelligence build-out have lost $4.2 trillion in value, with Nvidia's quarterly results this week and Anthropic's coming initial public offering the next two tests of the trade.
business_politics.summary: Money has rotated out of the "picks and shovels" suppliers that build, wire, and power data centers and into defensive sectors, the Financial Times found. Anthropic plans to sell shares to the public this month, and individual investors told the Wall Street Journal they feel compelled to buy a company whose technology they distrust, one describing the offering as "almost like the last chopper out of Saigon."

sources.title: Data centre construction stocks lose $4.2tn as boom in AI trade unravels
Will Nvidia earnings steady the AI sell-off?
Anthropic’s IPO is the next big test for AI
The Individual Investors Who Are Hot on Anthropic’s IPO But Cool on AI

business_politics.title: Congress Moves on Chip Exports
business_politics.latest_developments: Jensen Huang has discussed a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive with allies who now lobby the board to reinstate him, the Financial Times reported Sunday, November 15, hours after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded a "shake-up," urged the company to hire an outsider, and questioned whether Nvidia pushed illicit China sales to lift revenue.
business_politics.summary: Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on November 12, and finance chief Colette Kress runs the company while the board searches for a successor. Congress moves to pass tighter export controls on artificial-intelligence chips, and the Wall Street Journal reported that the enormous data centers Nvidia helped stand up in Southeast Asia fed Chinese companies crucial computing power and gave cover to alleged chip smuggling.

sources.title: Congress moves to pass tighter AI chip export rules following Nvidia scandal
How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race

business_politics.title: Iran Hits Bahrain a Second Time This Week
business_politics.latest_developments: Bahrain said Sunday, November 15, that it destroyed a second barrage of Iranian drones in a week, American estimates now put Tehran's rebuilt missile stockpile at as many as 2,500, and The Economist reported the same day that six men from a council of generals and bureaucrats run Iran in the absence of a supreme leader.
business_politics.summary: Iran has struck the island kingdom, which hosts the United States Navy's Fifth Fleet, repeatedly since the war with Washington began, and this week's attacks break months of relative calm in the Gulf. The missile figure contradicts President Trump's public assertions and feeds the administration's debate over resuming strikes.

sources.title: Iran attacks Bahrain in escalation of Gulf hostilities
Iran Targets Bahrain Again After Resuming Attacks on U.S. Ally

business_politics.title: One Router in Southern Arkansas
business_politics.latest_developments: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy spent Sunday, November 15, on the airwaves defending his decision to ground thousands of flights and pressing Congress for billions of dollars, as airlines canceled hundreds more departures in a third straight day of disruption.
business_politics.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration halted every departing flight in the country Friday afternoon, November 13, stalling hundreds of thousands of travelers, and the Wall Street Journal traced the collapse to a single router in southern Arkansas that a data overload knocked out on an antiquated agency network. Investigators have centered on the contractor L3Harris and a job replacing copper wire, and the Financial Times reported that decades of bipartisan neglect left the pilot-controller communications system unfit for its job.

sources.title: Ground Stop Ripples Into Third Day of Scrapped Flights
The Single Router in Southern Arkansas That Ground Air Travel to a Halt

business.title: Faucher Likes the Holiday Sales Outlook
business.latest_developments: Gus Faucher used his Economist's View column in the Post-Gazette on Sunday, November 15, to argue that the outlook for holiday sales looks good despite the gloom around consumers.
business.summary: Faucher, the chief economist at Pittsburgh-based PNC Financial Services Group, writes the Post-Gazette's Economist's View column, and his read on household spending sets expectations for Western Pennsylvania retailers heading into Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26.

sources.title: Economist’s View: Believe it or not, outlook looks good for holiday sales

business.title: The $1.7 Billion Terminal at One Year
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette asked Sunday, November 15, whether Pittsburgh International Airport's $1.7 billion terminal, now one year old, earned its price.
business.summary: The Allegheny County Airport Authority opened the building in November 2025, moving ticketing, security screening, and baggage claim next to the gates in Findlay Township. Its first anniversary weekend brought dozens of cancellations and delays as the airport dug out from the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop.

sources.title: One year in: Was the new Pittsburgh International Airport terminal worth building?

around_town.title: Sister Bridges Close for Lighting Repairs
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Sunday, November 15, that temporary closures begin on Pittsburgh's Sister Bridges at the start of this week for lighting repairs.
around_town.summary: The three spans—the Roberto Clemente, Andy Warhol, and Rachel Carson bridges—carry traffic over the Allegheny River between downtown and the North Shore, and crews need the decks clear to work on their lighting.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's Sister Bridges to be temporarily closed for lighting repairs

around_town.title: The United States Loses Measles Elimination Status
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA reported Sunday, November 15, that the United States has lost its official measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years.
around_town.summary: A country holds elimination status by going a year without continuous transmission of the virus, and this year's outbreaks ended that streak. Pennsylvania sits inside the count: the state Department of Health has confirmed 1,542 cases across 46 of the commonwealth's 67 counties and seven deaths this year.

sources.title: The U.S. has lost measles elimination status. Here's what that means and who is most at risk.

around_town.title: Pittsburgh International Digs Out
around_town.latest_developments: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday, November 15, that the government will pin down the "root cause" of the breakdown before it makes broad fixes to air traffic control, President Trump broke his silence on the collapse, and airlines canceled hundreds more flights nationwide in a third day of disruption.
around_town.summary: Pittsburgh International Airport ran dozens of cancellations and delays through the weekend as crews and airlines rebuilt schedules wrecked by Friday's nationwide ground stop, and KDKA's Ricky Sayer reported from the terminal in Findlay Township on a day travelers spent rebooking and waiting. The Federal Aviation Administration grounded every departing United States flight Friday afternoon, November 13, after communications failed at regional air traffic control centers.

sources.title: Pittsburgh International Airport sees dozens of cancellations, delays as airport rebounds from FAA ground stop
Nationwide ground stop: Travel expected to recover before weekend is over
Transportation head vows to find ‘root cause’ of ground stop. Trump breaks his silence on breakdown

around_town.title: The Lake-Effect Stretch Ends
around_town.latest_developments: Spotty showers wound down over the Pittsburgh area Sunday evening, November 15, with temperatures falling into the 30s overnight, and WTAE has the workweek turning sunny and warmer after a cloudy, chilly Monday.
around_town.summary: KDKA meteorologist Mary Ours opened Sunday with chilly temperatures and scattered snow showers, and WPXI reported that a few flakes mixed in around the city while the steadier snow fell over the Laurel Highlands and the Allegheny Mountains.

around_town.title: What Sports Betting Has Done to Young Men Here
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published an account Sunday, November 15, of how sports betting has reshaped the finances and habits of young men across Western Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: The piece lands as wagering runs through every Steelers broadcast, including Sunday night's game at Cincinnati, and follows PublicSource's finding last week that Pennsylvania's self-exclusion rolls now reach far beyond the counties that host casinos.

sources.title: How sports betting has impacted young men’s lives in Western Pa.

events.title: Richard Sterban Dies at 83
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Saturday, November 14, that Richard Sterban, the bass vocalist of The Oak Ridge Boys, has died at 83.
events.summary: Sterban sang the bottom line of the country and gospel quartet's harmonies for more than five decades on record and on tour, a voice familiar to anyone who heard the group on country radio.

sources.title: Richard Sterban, bass vocalist of celebrated country and gospel group The Oak Ridge Boys, dies at 83

events.title: Richard Lloyd Dies at 75
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, that Richard Lloyd, the Pittsburgh native who played guitar for the New York band Television, has died at 75.
events.summary: Lloyd grew up in Pittsburgh and built his name downtown at CBGB in Manhattan, where Television's twin-guitar sound, captured on the 1977 album "Marquee Moon," shaped American rock for the next half century.

sources.title: Richard Lloyd, Pittsburgh native and guitarist for acclaimed NYC rockers Television, dies at 75

events.title: Pittsburgh on Screen in 'How to Rob a Bank'
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, November 13, that Pittsburgh plays a starring role in the new film "How to Rob a Bank."
events.summary: The production joins a long run of movies that use Pittsburgh's bridges, hillsides, and downtown blocks as more than a backdrop, and the Post-Gazette walks through the locations city audiences will recognize.

sources.title: In ‘How to Rob a Bank,’ Pittsburgh plays a starring role

around_teams.title: Scouting Cincinnati's Offense
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published its Week 10 scouting report Sunday, November 15, concluding that stopping what it calls Cincinnati's supermen on offense decides the game at Paycor Stadium.
around_teams.summary: The report measures the Bengals' personnel against a Steelers defense built to take away explosive plays, and Christopher Carter ran the Post-Gazette's live chat, updates, and analysis through the 8:20 p.m. Eastern kickoff on NBC with first place in the AFC North at stake.

around_teams.title: Explosive Passes Meet Pittsburgh's Secondary
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette examined Sunday, November 15, the central collision of the Steelers' trip to Cincinnati: the Bengals thrive on explosive passing plays, and the Steelers defense excels at stopping them.
around_teams.summary: Joe Burrow throws the deep ball that has carried Cincinnati's offense, and Pittsburgh brings the league's answer to it into Paycor Stadium for an 8:20 p.m. Eastern kickoff on NBC. Mike McCarthy previewed the Week 10 game with Bob Pompeani and the Steelers Insider panel on the team's channel Saturday night, November 14.

team_usa.title: The U.S. Meets Canada for the World Title
team_usa.latest_developments: The United States shut out Finland 5-0 Sunday, November 15, at the women's ice hockey world championship in Denmark, and Canada beat Sweden 3-0 the same day, setting the final for Monday, November 16.
team_usa.summary: The defending champion Americans came through the preliminary round unbeaten, with Hilary Knight's hat trick against the Czech Republic and a 14-0 win over host Denmark on Friday, November 13. They now play Canada for the title, the matchup the tournament has produced almost every year.

team_usa.title: Kansas City and Washington Reach the NWSL Final
team_usa.latest_developments: Haley Hopkins scored late Sunday, November 15, to beat the defending champion Gotham FC 2-1 and send the Kansas City Current into the National Women's Soccer League Championship against the Washington Spirit.
team_usa.summary: The Spirit, owned by Michele Kang, came from behind to beat the Utah Royals 2-1 Saturday, November 14, reaching a third straight final, and the club hosts the championship next week.

team_usa.title: Pochettino's Farewell Begins
team_usa.latest_developments: Mauricio Pochettino said after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti, November 14, that the United States men's national team has an "amazing future," and ESPN reported Sunday that his players intend to carry his standards forward in the penultimate match of his tenure.
team_usa.summary: Pochettino leaves for Manchester United on November 17, and Steve Cherundolo takes the December camp on an interim basis; the return leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti closes out the Argentine's run. Christian Pulisic scored twice in the first leg and drew a 9 out of 10 in ESPN's player ratings, and teenage forward Julian Hall tied himself to the United States over Poland by starting.

team_usa.title: Malinin Wins a Fourth Skate America
team_usa.latest_developments: Ilia Malinin won Skate America for the fourth time Saturday night, November 14, opening what ESPN calls a four-year run toward the 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps.
team_usa.summary: Malinin, 21, scored 96.74 points in Friday's short program to lead his first Grand Prix outing of the season, and he built that program as a tribute to the members of the skating community killed in January 2025 when their American Airlines flight collided with a military helicopter near Washington.

team_usa.title: Harrison's Case for the UFC
team_usa.latest_developments: Bryan Armen Graham argued in the Guardian on Sunday, November 15, that Kayla Harrison's career makes the UFC hard to dismiss even as the company squeezes fighters, bullies journalists, and courts President Trump.
team_usa.summary: Harrison won Olympic judo gold for the United States in 2012 and 2016, sports that paid their champions almost nothing, and she now headlines for a promotion that gave athletes from neglected Olympic disciplines a route to real money and fame. Trump publicly floated UFC Chief Executive Dana White for a role in his administration last week.
